findings.description: `indent=self.indent` is now always passed to every exporter class. A user exporter registered in FEED_EXPORTERS whose __init__ doesn't accept an `indent` keyword (and doesn't forward **kwargs to _configure) will now raise TypeError, even though the user never set FEED_EXPORT_INDENT. Consider passing indent only when it's set, or handling exporters that don't accept it.

With indent > 0, a field whose value is an empty dict or empty list is written as `<foo>\n      </foo>` instead of `<foo></foo>`, because the newline and closing indent are added whatever the container holds. Pretty-printing also puts whitespace text nodes into element content, which changes the XML data for anyone who reads it with whitespace preserved.

FEED_EXPORT_INDENT = 0 changes the default XML feed output: newlines now appear after <items> and after each <item>. Existing users who compare or parse the exact output will see this change, and it isn't mentioned as backward-incompatible.

The docs contradict themselves. They say a 'non-negative integer' enables pretty-printing, then say 0 only puts each item on a new line. It should say 'positive integer'. The sentence about None is also missing its final period.
Typos: "it's" should be "its" and "indentated" should be "indented". The documented default (0) also doesn't match the code (None).
Typo in the comment: 'behaviour or' should be 'behaviour of'.
A debug `print(row['format'], row['indent'])` was left in the test loop. Remove it, or use the case as the assertion message instead.

You can't set FEED_EXPORT_INDENT to None from the command line (`-s FEED_EXPORT_INDENT=None`): the value arrives as the string 'None', and getint raises ValueError. The compact mode can only be selected through Python settings.
